public import FormalConjecturesUtil
/-!

# Erdős Problem 354
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/354](https://www.erdosproblems.com/354)

-/

@[expose] public section
namespace Erdos354

/-- The sequence `⌊a⌋, ⌊γ * a⌋, ⌊γ ^ 2 * a⌋, ..., ⌊γ ^ i * a⌋, ...`. -/
noncomputable def FloorMultiples (a γ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ := ⌊γ ^ n * a⌋

/-- The sequence `⌊a⌋, ⌊b⌋, ⌊γ * a⌋, ⌊γ * b⌋, ... ⌊γ ^ i * a⌋, ⌊γ ^ i * b⌋, ...` -/
noncomputable def FloorMultiples.interleave (a b γ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if n % 2 = 0 then
    FloorMultiples a γ (n / 2)
  else
    FloorMultiples b γ (n / 2)

/-- Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is the multiset
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 2\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 4\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor 2\beta\rfloor,\lfloor 4\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) →
    IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β 2) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma^2\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma\beta\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma^2\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2, ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) →
    IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β γ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos354

findings.description:
The Lean statement is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ γ ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2, ∀ α > 0, ∀ β > 0, Irrational (α / β) → IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (interleave α β γ)`. It asks whether there is at least one base γ ∈ (1,2) for which the analogue of part (i) holds.

The source's follow-up question is different. It asks whether the conclusion survives when the base 2 is replaced by an arbitrary γ with 1<γ<2 (universal in γ, or 'for which γ').

The existential version is weak enough to be provable by an elementary argument with γ = φ (golden ratio). Write a_n = ⌊φ^n x⌋. Since φ^{n+2} = φ^{n+1} + φ^n, we have a_{n+2} ∈ {a_{n+1}+a_n, a_{n+1}+a_n+1}.
1. For the α-sequence, a_n ≤ K + Σ_{i<n} a_i with K = a_0 + a_1 + 1.
2. For the β-sequence, the '+1' carry occurs infinitely often. Otherwise e_n = φ^nβ − b_n ∈ [0,1) would satisfy e_{n+2} = e_{n+1} + e_n from some point on, forcing e_n → ∞ or φ ∈ ℚ. So k well-separated carries make k+1 consecutive integers X..X+k sums of distinct β-terms.
3. Adding the α-terms one at a time extends [X, X+K] to [X, ∞).

Hence the interleaving is complete for every α, β > 0; the irrationality hypothesis is never used.

I proved this in Lean in about 260 lines (/workspace/review/partii.lean). `example : type_of% @Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.ii := ⟨fun _ => parts_ii_rhs, fun _ => trivial⟩` compiles with 0 errors, and its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. So the declared 'research open' theorem is provable, with answer True.

The literature reads the question universally and answers it the other way. Geneson (arXiv:2609.25107) builds a Salem number γ ∈ (6/5, 13/10) and α, β > 0 with α/β irrational such that every term of both sequences is even, so the interleaving is incomplete. So the file's statement is 'yes', while the source's question is 'no' (per that preprint).

Graham posed this knowing his own 1964 lemma, which settles the existential version at once. That shows the ∃ reading is not the intended question.
findings.source_evidence:
Graham 1971, 'On sums of integers taken from a fixed sequence', Question 12 (p.36): "Let α and β be positive reals with α/β irrational. Let S denote the sequence ([α], [β], [2α], [2β], ..., [2^nα], [2^nβ], ...). Is S complete? What if 2 is replaced by some γ, 1 < γ < 2?"

Erdős–Graham 1980, p.58: "... Is S complete? What if 2 is replaced by γ where 1 < γ < 2?"

erdosproblems.com/354: "What if 2 is replaced by some γ∈(1,2)?"

Geneson, arXiv:2609.25107, Sec. 'Two sequences with a common base', quoting ErGr80: "'What if 2 is replaced by γ where 1<γ<2?' ... Our example gives an incomplete interleaving for some such bases". The introduction adds: "This answers negatively the variable-base extension of the two-sequence question in Graham [Question 12, p. 36] and Erdős and Graham [p. 58]. It does not resolve the original base-2 question, recorded as Erdős Problem 354."

On the erdosproblems forum, van Doorn discusses partial results for particular ranges of γ (e.g. γ = √2, 1<γ≤√2). That only makes sense under the universal / 'for which γ' reading.
findings.suggested_fix:
Quantify γ universally, and state γ ∈ (1,2) in the docstring:

@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2, ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0),
    Irrational (α / β) → IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β γ) := by
  sorry

Per arXiv:2609.25107 this would become `research solved` with `answer(False)` once vetted.

Alternatively, ask 'for which γ': `{γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2 | ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) → IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β γ)} = answer(sorry)`. This form stays open: φ is in the set and Geneson's Salem γ is not.

The existential statement can be kept as a separate solved variant (witness γ = φ).

findings.description: The docstring never introduces γ. It reads "Let α,β∈ℝ>0 such that α/β is irrational. Is {⌊α⌋,⌊γα⌋,…}∪{⌊β⌋,⌊γβ⌋,…} complete?" and states neither the source's range γ ∈ (1,2) nor any quantifier. The Lean, meanwhile, has `∃ γ ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2`. A reader cannot tell from the docstring what the theorem asserts about γ.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/354: "What if 2 is replaced by some γ∈(1,2)?"; ErGr80 p.58: "What if 2 is replaced by γ where 1 < γ < 2?"
findings.suggested_fix: State the variant explicitly, e.g. "Let α,β>0 with α/β irrational. Is the multiset {⌊γ^nα⌋} ∪ {⌊γ^nβ⌋} complete for every γ ∈ (1,2)?" (matching the corrected Lean).

status_issues.source_status: The variable-base (γ ∈ (1,2)) extension has been answered negatively under the universal reading. J. Geneson, arXiv:2609.25107 (submitted 20 Sep 2026), Corollary on two sequences with a common base: take γ to be the Salem root of x^18−x^12−…−x^6+1 in (6/5,13/10), and set α = 2ηγ, β = α(1+γ). Then every term of both sequences is even, α/β is irrational, and the interleaving is incomplete. erdosproblems.com/354 still marks the problem (the base-2 question) OPEN and does not yet mention this. Separately, the existential statement as currently written is provable (answer True; my Lean proof with γ = φ).
status_issues.evidence: arXiv:2609.25107 abstract: "For a common base in this range, we further construct two such sequences whose interleaving is incomplete and whose coefficient ratio is not a rational multiple of any integer power of the base." Introduction: "This answers negatively the variable-base extension of the two-sequence question in Graham [Question 12, p. 36] and Erdős and Graham [p. 58]. It does not resolve the original base-2 question, recorded as Erdős Problem 354." I checked the elementary deduction and P(1) = −5, 5^18·P(6/5) < 0 < 10^18·P(13/10).
status_issues.suggested_change: After correcting the quantifier to ∀ γ ∈ (1,2), change to `@[category research solved]` with `answer(False)`, citing arXiv:2609.25107 (the maintainers may prefer to wait until the preprint is vetted). If an existential variant is kept, it must be `research solved` with `answer(True)`. If the 'for which γ' set version is adopted instead, it remains open.

reformulations.difference: The source works with the union of the two sequences and asks that all sufficiently large natural numbers be n = Σ_{s∈S}⌊2^sα⌋ + Σ_{t∈T}⌊2^tβ⌋ for finite S, T. The Lean instead encodes the union as one interleaved sequence `FloorMultiples.interleave α β 2 : ℕ → ℤ` (even index 2s ↦ ⌊2^sα⌋, odd index 2t+1 ↦ ⌊2^tβ⌋). It expresses completeness as `∀ᶠ k in atTop` on ℤ of membership in `subseqSums'`, i.e. sums over finite index sets, so repeated values are counted with multiplicity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite index set B corresponds bijectively to the pair (S, T) = ((even part of B)/2, (odd part of B)/2), and the sums agree. I proved in Lean (/workspace/review/reform.lean, 0 errors) that `subseqSums' (interleave a b γ) = {n | ∃ S T : Finset ℕ, n = ∑ s ∈ S, ⌊γ^s*a⌋ + ∑ t ∈ T, ⌊γ^t*b⌋}`. From it I proved that part (i)'s right-hand side is ↔ `∀ α>0, ∀ β>0, Irrational (α/β) → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ S T, n = ∑…+∑…`. 'Eventually in atTop on ℤ' is the same as 'all sufficiently large naturals'. Index sets keep multiplicities, matching the source's 'multiset' and ErGr80's P(A) = {Σ ε_k a_k : ε_k ∈ {0,1}}. Index 0 (⌊α⌋, ⌊β⌋) is included, as in the source's listed multiset. Even if the source's ℕ excluded 0, the universal statement would be unchanged: rescaling α, β by 2 preserves the hypotheses.

could_not_verify: Geneson's negative answer to the universal γ-variant (arXiv:2609.25107). I checked the elementary steps: the sign adjustment, that all terms are even, that α/β is irrational, and the interval (6/5,13/10) containing the root of P. I did not check Dubickas's theorem (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), Thm 6), on which the existence of η with 3/20 < {ηγ^n} < 1/4 rests. This affects only the status note, not the misformalization finding: the existential statement's provability is Lean-verified on its own.
Hegyvári (1989), 'Some remarks on a problem of Erdős and Graham' (Acta Math. Hungar. 53) was not accessible. Its contents are known to me only through Hegyvári 1991 and the erdosproblems page.

not_demonstrated.reason: Provable as stated (answer True, witness γ = φ), but only through a real argument: the floor recurrence, infinitely many carries from φ's irrationality, runs of consecutive subset sums, and Graham's Σ-sequence lemma. That is about 260 lines of Lean (/workspace/review/partii.lean, compiles, standard axioms), not a few lines. The negation is false, so there is no short disproof.

submission.summary: I did not create a trivial-proof file. The misformalized declaration Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.ii has a Lean proof of about 260 lines with γ = φ (/workspace/review/partii.lean, 0 errors, standard axioms only). It shows the 'research open' existential statement is provable, but the argument is genuine mathematics rather than a few-line demonstration. Since the statement is true, there is no disproof to give.
submission.gave_up_reason: The one reported misformalization, Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.ii (∃ γ ∈ (1,2) where the source means every γ), makes the statement true, so there is no disproof. The only proof I have is not short. With γ = φ it combines four steps: the floor recurrence ⌊φ^{n+2}x⌋ ∈ {⌊φ^{n+1}x⌋+⌊φ^n x⌋, same+1}; infinitely many '+1' carries, which uses the irrationality of φ; assembling carries into arbitrarily long runs of consecutive subset sums; and Graham's Σ-sequence induction to reach all large integers. This took about 260 lines of Lean (/workspace/review/partii.lean). It compiles with 0 errors, depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and checks `type_of% @Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.ii` directly. No witness γ shortens this, because any proof must handle arbitrary α, β > 0. FormalConjecturesForMathlib has no completeness criterion (Brown/Graham) to reuse either. Under the rules, a proof needing real mathematics is not a trivial demonstration, so I did not create trivial_proof.lean.

submission.summary: Changed `erdos_354.parts.ii` from `∃ γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2` to `∀ γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2`, matching the source's variable-base question as Graham (1971), Erdős–Graham (1980) and Geneson (arXiv:2609.25107) read it. The old existential version is provable with γ = φ. Rewrote the docstring to quote the source's question and state the universal reading with γ ∈ (1,2); this also fixes the minor docstring item, since γ was never introduced before. Nothing else in the file changed. The file compiles with only the two `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. A copy of the edited file shows the new statement elaborates to `True ↔ ∀ γ ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2, ∀ α > 0, ∀ β > 0, Irrational (α / β) → IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (interleave α β γ)`, which implies the old statement and has satisfiable hypotheses (γ = 3/2, α = 1, β = √2). The tag stays `research open` with `answer(sorry)`, because erdosproblems.com still lists the problem as open. Geneson's preprint (20 Sep 2026) gives a counterexample, so maintainers may switch to `research solved` with `answer(False)` once it is vetted. I did not add a solved existential variant; the Lean proof with γ = φ is in /workspace/review/partii.lean if wanted. No other file under /opt/formal-conjectures was modified by me.
